title: amele agent configuration
description: The single YAML file that defines an amele agent: model, provider endpoint, prompts, tools, budgets and output contract. Any string value may contain ${ENV_VAR} references, which amele substitutes from the process environment at load time (write $$ for a literal $); this schema mostly describes the shape after that interpolation. Integer and duration fields additionally accept a whole-value ${VAR} reference, because filling budgets from the environment is the normal headless/cron idiom. Known editor-time limitation: boolean fields (e.g. tools.fs) and enum fields (provider.type, permission policies) remain strictly typed here, so a ${VAR} placeholder in those is flagged by editors even though amele itself would accept and interpolate it. Unknown keys are rejected at load time, mirrored here by additionalProperties: false.

model.description: Model identifier sent to the provider, e.g. "gpt-4.1-mini" or "openai/gpt-5.6-luna". Required unless overridden on the command line with --model.

provider.description: The LLM endpoint the agent talks to: an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API (the default), the native Anthropic Messages API, or the native Google Gemini API, selected by type.

type.description: Wire protocol: "openai" for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (also the meaning when omitted), "anthropic" for the native Anthropic Messages API, "gemini" for the native Google Gemini generateContent API. Each is its own wire family, not a variation of another: dialect describes the openai wire only.

base_url.description: API root, e.g. "https://api.openai.com/v1". Required for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. With type "anthropic" it may be omitted (the client defaults to the official endpoint) and must NOT end with /v1 - the client appends /v1/messages itself. With type "gemini" it may likewise be omitted (the client defaults to the fixed Gemini API host); a value overrides the host for proxied deployments.

api_key.description: Credential for the provider - the Authorization bearer token on the openai wire, the x-api-key header with type "anthropic", the x-goog-api-key header with type "gemini". Must be built only from environment references (api_key: ${MY_API_KEY}); literal secrets in YAML are rejected at load time. An empty key is valid for local endpoints such as Ollama.

request_timeout.description: Upper bound for a single HTTP round-trip to the provider, e.g. "120s". Empty or omitted means the client default (120s). Distinct from limits.timeout, which bounds the whole run: slow reasoning models can need several minutes for one generation.

max_output_tokens.description: Per-request output token ceiling. 0 (or omitted) sends no cap and leaves the provider default in force. Honored on both paths: the Anthropic API requires the field, and on the OpenAI wire the dialect picks the field name (max_completion_tokens or max_tokens). Reasoning tokens count against this ceiling wherever a provider reports them, so leave room for the thinking as well as the answer. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

dialect.description: Variation of the OpenAI-compatible wire format this endpoint speaks, which decides how reasoning, sampling and the output cap are mapped onto the request. Omitted means "openai", the baseline. It is explicit rather than guessed from base_url: a wrong guess would send a knob to the wrong field name and surface only as a provider error later. Ignored when type is "anthropic", and rejected at load time when type is "gemini" - that is a different wire family, so a dialect there would name a mapping the request never takes.

reasoning.description: Provider-neutral thinking knob. An absent block means the config never asks - which is NOT the same as asking for "none": most reasoning models think by default and several cannot be switched off. `amele explain` reports how the values map onto the chosen dialect, including any rounding.

effort.description: Reasoning depth - the union of the vocabularies the supported providers accept; no single provider accepts all six, so a dialect without an equivalent rounds the value to the nearest one it has (visibly, in explain). Omitted sends no knob and the provider default applies.

budget_tokens.description: Caps the thinking with a token count instead of a level. 0 (or omitted) means unset. Only budget-based targets can carry it: type "anthropic", type "gemini" (thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget), or dialect "openrouter" (which converts it). Anywhere else it is a config error rather than a silently dropped field. With type "gemini" it is an ALTERNATIVE to effort, never a companion: setting both is a config error, because the Gemini API refuses a request carrying thinkingLevel and thinkingBudget together. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Omitted means the provider decides; 0 is a value, not "unset". The target can narrow the range - type "anthropic" and dialect "glm" both accept only 0..1, and dialect "kimi" (openai wire only) rejects temperature and top_p outright because its K-series models fix them - all enforced at load time. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling, greater than 0 and at most 1. Omitted means the provider decides. Rejected outright on the kimi dialect (openai wire only), whose K-series models fix sampling. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

retry.description: How a transient provider failure is retried. WHICH failures are retried is not configurable: 429, 5xx and network errors are transient by definition, and anything else is a request the provider would refuse just as firmly on the next attempt. An absent block means the client defaults (3 attempts, 1s initial backoff).

max_attempts.description: Total tries for one provider call (1 initial + retries), so 1 disables retrying. 0 (or omitted) means the default 3; values above 10 are a config error. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

initial_backoff.description: Wait before the second attempt, doubled for each attempt after that, e.g. "200ms". Empty or omitted means the default (1s); accepted range 100ms..60s, enforced at load time. A provider's Retry-After header still stretches an individual wait (capped at 60s).

vertex.description: Points the gemini wire at Vertex AI instead of the AI Studio host: the request goes to https://{location}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model}:generateContent (host without the region prefix when location is "global"), authenticated with Google credentials rather than an API key. Valid only with type "gemini", and never together with api_key - Vertex refuses API keys outright. An absent block means AI Studio.

project.description: Google Cloud project id (or project number) that owns the quota and billing for the request. Required. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: it travels as a path segment of the endpoint.

location.description: Vertex location: a region id ("us-central1", "europe-west4"), a jurisdictional multi-region ("us", "eu"), or "global". Required, and never defaulted or rewritten - it decides where the prompt is processed, which is a data-residency commitment. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: it becomes part of the endpoint host. Model availability is per-location, so a model absent from the chosen location fails loudly instead of being rerouted.

credentials.description: Path to a service-account key file. Omitted means Application Default Credentials: the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS variable, then gcloud's user credentials, then the metadata server.

params.description: Escape hatch: arbitrary keys merged verbatim into the request body root, for provider extras amele has no neutral field for (e.g. verbosity, or OpenRouter's provider routing block). Keys amele writes itself ON THE ACTIVE TARGET are rejected at load time - model, messages, tools, response_format, temperature, top_p, the dialect's cap and reasoning spellings, thinking/output_config/system on the anthropic wire, and contents/systemInstruction/tools/toolConfig/generationConfig/safetySettings/cachedContent (in either spelling) on the gemini wire - so params can extend a request but never rewrite one. stream and tool_choice are refused everywhere: amele's transport reads a single JSON body and its loop owns the tool protocol. A key the active target never writes (thinking on kimi) stays available. Values must be JSON-serializable.

system_prompt.description: Inline system prompt for the agent. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt_file.

system_prompt_file.description: Path to a file holding the system prompt, resolved relative to the config file. Keeps long prompts out of the YAML. Mutually exclusive with system_prompt.

prompt.description: User-message template. May reference {{args}} (task text from the command line) and {{input}} (piped stdin). Omitted means a sensible default combining both.

workspace.description: Directory sandbox for the fs tools and working directory for subprocess and shell tools. Relative paths are resolved against the config file's directory, which is also the default.

tools.description: Selects which builtin tools are enabled and declares custom subprocess tools.

fs.description: Enables the builtin sandboxed filesystem tools (fs_read/fs_write/fs_list). They cannot reach outside the workspace.

shell.description: The builtin `shell` tool, which runs a model-written command line through `sh -c` in the workspace. Absent means disabled. SECURITY: allow/deny patterns are accident prevention, not a security boundary - the boundary is the OS/container the agent runs in.

enabled.description: Turns the shell tool on. Default (false) means the model has no shell; nothing else can enable it.

allow.description: Glob patterns (`*` matches any substring) matched against the whole command string. An empty list allows everything Deny does not catch; a non-empty list requires at least one match.

deny.description: Glob patterns checked BEFORE allow. Any match rejects the command.

env.description: Environment allowlist for shell commands. When non-empty, the child process is started with ONLY the listed variables (plus PATH, HOME and LANG, which are always passed so basic tools keep working); values are taken from amele's own environment and listed names that are unset are silently skipped. Empty or omitted means the child inherits amele's entire environment. SECURITY: this reduces credential exposure to model-written commands, but the boundary remains the OS/container the agent runs in.

timeout.description: Upper bound for a single shell command, e.g. "60s". Empty or omitted means the default (60s).

parallel.description: Whether the tool calls of ONE model turn may run at the same time. Default true: independent calls (three reads, two searches) finish in one round instead of N. The recorded order never changes - session events, message history and progress lines stay in the model's call order - and a turn that contains an `ask` permission falls back to one call at a time so approval prompts cannot interleave. Set false when tools are not independent (two tools writing the same file, a server that serializes badly).

subprocess.description: Custom executable tools. Each command is a fixed argv vector - no shell is involved, so the model can never inject into a shell string.

name.description: Tool name exposed to the model. Restricted to letters, digits, `_` and `-` (max 64 chars). The builtin names fs_read, fs_write, fs_list and shell are reserved.

description.description: Tells the model what the tool does and when to use it. Required - an undescribed tool is unusable to the model.

command.description: Argv vector to execute; the first element is the executable and must be non-empty. The model writes to the process's stdin and reads its stdout. Path-like relative commands (containing a path separator, e.g. ./tools/scan.sh) resolve against the config file's directory; bare names resolve from PATH.

timeout.description: Upper bound for a single invocation, e.g. "30s". Empty or omitted means the default (60s).

allow_args.description: Lets the model append extra argv elements after command. SECURITY: disabled by default - with it off the model controls stdin only, never the argument vector.

env.description: Environment allowlist for this tool's process. When non-empty, the child is started with ONLY the listed variables (plus PATH, HOME and LANG, which are always passed so basic tools keep working); values are taken from amele's own environment and listed names that are unset are silently skipped. Empty or omitted means the child inherits amele's entire environment. SECURITY: this reduces credential exposure to model-driven commands, but the boundary remains the OS/container the agent runs in.

limits.description: Run budgets - the kill switches that make an agent safe to leave unattended in cron. Exceeding any of them ends the run with exit code 3.

max_turns.description: Upper bound on provider round-trips. 0 (or omitted) means the default (20). May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

max_tokens.description: Upper bound on cumulative input+output tokens as reported by the provider - the primary budget unit. 0 (or omitted) disables the token budget. May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

timeout.description: Wall-clock bound for the whole run (`amele run`) or for one exchange (`amele chat`), e.g. "5m". Empty or omitted disables it.

session_dir.description: Enables append-only JSONL session logging into this directory when non-empty. Relative paths are resolved against the config file's directory. Interpolated environment values are redacted from the log.

lock.description: Makes `amele run` single-flight per config file: it takes a non-blocking advisory lock on "<config path>.lock" before contacting the provider, and a run that finds the lock held exits with code 7 without doing anything. Only run locks - validate, explain and chat never do. Default false (opt-in), so the same config can still be run concurrently with different tasks; cron jobs that must not overlap themselves set it to true.

output.description: Constrains the run's final answer to a JSON Schema. With a schema set, stdout carries only JSON that validated against it, and a run whose answers never validate exits with code 6.

schema.description: Inline JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 by default) written as a YAML mapping. External $ref targets are rejected - inline everything with $defs. Empty or omitted means no constraint: the final answer is plain text.

max_schema_retries.description: How many times the model receives validator feedback before the run fails with exit 6. 0 (or omitted) means the default (2). May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

permissions.description: Per-run tool approval profile: one fallback policy plus per-tool overrides. An absent block allows every tool. With no TTY attached, every "ask" degrades to a logged denial.

default.description: Policy applied to any tool without an entry in tools. Omitted means allow.

tools.description: Maps a tool name to its policy, overriding default. A key may contain * and then matches by pattern (e.g. github__*); an exact key wins over any pattern, and among matching patterns the most restrictive policy wins (deny > ask > allow). Entries for tools that do not exist in this config are inert, so profiles can be shared across configs.

mcp.description: MCP servers whose tools are offered to the model as <server>__<tool>. The block is top level rather than under tools because one connection may later also carry resources and prompts.

servers.description: Declared MCP connections, in file order. Server names must be unique and must not collide with a builtin or subprocess tool name.

name.description: Prefix of every tool this server contributes ("<name>__<tool>"). Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, max 32 chars - stricter than a subprocess tool name because the model must type the full prefixed name back verbatim.

transport.description: How to reach the server. Which other fields are legal depends on type; mixing them is a config error rather than a silently ignored key.

type.description: "stdio" runs the server as a child process and speaks JSON-RPC over its stdin/stdout; "http" talks to a remote server over streamable HTTP. Required - there is no default.

url.description: Endpoint for type http. Must use https unless the host is loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1): on the open network plain http is a plaintext credential and an unauthenticated instruction channel.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for type http. Credential-shaped names (authorization, cookie, or any name containing key/token/secret/passw/cred) must be built from ${ENV_VAR} references and are redacted from logs; headers amele manages itself (Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Accept, Mcp-Session-Id, MCP-Protocol-Version, Last-Event-ID) are rejected.

command.description: Argv vector for type stdio; the first element is the executable and must be non-empty. Path-like relative commands (containing a path separator, e.g. ./tools/srv) resolve against the config file's directory; bare names resolve from PATH.

env.description: Environment allowlist for a stdio server's child process: names, never assignments. Unlike a subprocess tool's env, empty or omitted means the MINIMAL environment - PATH, HOME and LANG only; amele's other variables (including the provider API key) reach the server only when named here.

tools.description: Narrows the tool set this server contributes. Patterns match the server-side tool name, before the "<server>__" prefix is added.

include.description: Glob patterns a tool must match to be exposed. Empty or omitted means every tool.

exclude.description: Glob patterns that remove a tool include let through. Applied after include.

call_timeout.description: Upper bound for a single MCP tool call, e.g. "60s". Empty or omitted means the default (60s).

required.description: Whether a failure to connect aborts the run. Omitted means true: fail-fast is the default, because a headless run that silently loses half its tools produces a plausible wrong answer. Set false to let the run continue without this server.

auth.description: OAuth for this server. Requires transport.type http, and cannot be combined with an Authorization header on the same server. Omitted means static headers only.

type.description: Auth mechanism. "oauth" is the only accepted value: OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE.

client_id.description: Pre-registered OAuth client id. Omitted means client id metadata discovery, when the authorization server supports it. There is deliberately no client_secret: amele is a public client, and a secret in a recipe would be a committed credential.

scopes.description: Extra scopes, added (union) to the server-driven scope selection rather than replacing it.

duration.description: Go duration string: one or more number+unit segments, e.g. "30s", "5m", "1h30m", "1.5s". Units: ns, us (or µs), ms, s, m, h. Negative durations are rejected; an empty string means "use the default". May also be a whole-value ${VAR} environment reference resolved at load time.

policy.description: Permission ruling for a tool call: "allow" runs it without asking, "ask" prompts the human on the terminal (degrading to deny when no TTY is attached), "deny" refuses the call while the run continues with the remaining tools.
